key_insight: Holographic measurements revealed deformation and failure of detonation-sprayed natural-material coatings under intense heat loads, supporting assessment of thermal stability.
engineering_relevance: The findings can inform deposition conditions, cooling strategies, and protective-screen design for tuff and marble coatings exposed to high-temperature jets.
method: Varied oxidizer excess ratio, thermal-tool conditions, and coating material.
Recorded detonation-jet flame structure and coating deformation using holography.
Developed protective screens to prevent coating failure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports surface heat fluxes of 5–12 MW/m² at 0.04 m from the nozzle and a failure case with a 2.5 mm cavity forming within 2.2 s at 1.2 MW/m².
watch_item: Service-life prediction is proposed, but the abstract provides no long-term validation or uncertainty estimates.
paper_title: HOLOGRAPHIC INVESTIGATION OF THERMAL STABILITY OF COATINGS FROM NATURAL MATERIALS PRODUCED BY THE DETONATION METHOD
